primitives.name: Pass Hazard Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: (2016) multi-resolution possession model — possessions decompose into possession states (micro-movements), transition states (pass/shot/turnover), and end states (0/2/3 points); the pass hazard for carrier i to teammate j is the log-linear model (2): log(θ_{i,j}(t)) = W_{i,j}(t)^T η_{i,j} + ξ_{i,j}(s_i(t)) + ξ̃_{i,j}(s_j(t)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ_{i,j}(t)': 'pass intensity rate between players i and j at time t (dimensionless)', 'W_{i,j}(t)': 'covariate vector for pass event (dimensionless)', 'η_{i,j}': 'latent parameter vector (dimensionless)', 'ξ_{i,j}(s_i(t))': 'spatial effect for passer i at time t (dimensionless)', 'ξ̃_{i,j}(s_j(t))': 'spatial effect for receiver j at time t (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Passes modeled as non-homogeneous Poisson process with time-varying intensity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When spatial effects become negligible or when latent factors fail to capture interaction dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state transition kernel for receiver-target selection under pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Observed pass frequency and spatial clustering patterns.

primitives.name: Latent Sender-Receiver Factors
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Full model (SMOGS)** (7–10): passes as events of a non-homogeneous spatio-temporal Poisson process with game-specific latent factors: log(θ_{i,j}(t)) = X_{i,j}(t)^T β_{i,j} + **u_{i,g}^T v_{j,g}** + ε_{i,j}(t), where u_{i,g}, v_{j,g} are R-dimensional sender/receiver latent vectors for player i/j in game g
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ_{i,j}(t)': 'pass intensity rate between players i and j at time t (dimensionless)', 'X_{i,j}(t)': 'dyadic covariates (dimensionless)', 'β_{i,j}': 'regression coefficients (dimensionless)', 'u_{i,g}': 'sender latent vector for player i in game g (R-dimensional)', 'v_{j,g}': 'receiver latent vector for player j in game g (R-dimensional)', 'ε_{i,j}(t)': 'error term (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pass intensity depends linearly on observed covariates and multiplicative latent interaction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When latent dimensions R are insufficient to represent complex player dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to compute QB–WR chemistry scores via dot product of latent vectors.
layer2.telemetry: Chemistry score distributions across QB–WR pairs.

primitives.name: Spatial Smoothing Effects
primitives.verbatim_quote: Spatial effects ξ̄_i, ξ̃̄_{i,pos(j)} estimated off-line by **thin-plate-spline smoothing** of empirical pass-location counts on 1 ft × 1 ft half-court tiles (11), with λ chosen by generalized cross-validation — simpler and less data-hungry than the GMRF approach of Cervone et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ξ̄_i': 'spatial effect for passer i (dimensionless)', 'ξ̃̄_{i,pos(j)}': 'spatial effect for receiver j at position pos(i) (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Empirical pass locations follow smooth spatial distribution approximated by thin-plate splines.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pass locations are sparse or irregularly distributed.

layer2.mapping: Applied in GSE to refine pass probability maps based on court positioning.
layer2.telemetry: Pass location density maps and spatial clustering metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of SMOGS lies in modeling team passing as a dynamic social network through latent sender-receiver factors. The model assumes that pass events arise from a non-homogeneous Poisson process governed by both observed covariates and unobserved latent interactions. This allows for capturing nuanced team chemistry beyond simple statistics. The key innovation is the use of multiplicative latent factors u_i^T v_j which encode how well two players interact, enabling interpretation of win/loss outcomes via fragmentation vs. overlap of these latent effects. In GSE, this translates to computing QB–WR chemistry scores dynamically during gameplay, where the latent vectors reflect real-time coordination. The failure mode occurs when the latent space lacks sufficient expressive power to distinguish meaningful player pairings, leading to poor generalization. The model also introduces spatial smoothing to account for positional influence, which enhances robustness against noise in tracking data.
